executive_summary.description: When a parent container is resized by dragging its SE corner, the NW corner (the anchored corner) drifts in the same direction as the drag instead of staying fixed. The child node moves with the drifting NW corner, maintaining its relative offset within the container (so the child does NOT slide inside the container), but the whole container+child assembly translates visually. The result feels jarring because the child appears to jump toward the dragged corner.
executive_summary.affects: _htResizeApplyCompound in the inline canvas JS (largest inline script, ~62 KB)

child_displacement.verdict: JARRING — child moved ~82 CSS px for a 150 CSS px drag

secondary_tests.verdict: Symmetric bug — drift also occurs on contraction
SE corner also drifts when NW is dragged — bug is not corner-specific

root_cause_analysis.mechanism: For compound (parent) nodes, the resize logic repositions children relative to the NEW calculated container center (calc.position). It then sets min-width/min-height with directional bias properties to size the container. However, Cytoscape.js re-anchors the compound node's bounding box around the repositioned children, and the directional bias is applied relative to the children's NEW center (which has already moved), not the original fixed corner. Net effect: the supposedly-anchored corner slips by approximately half the delta for corner drags, because the child was moved to the new center before the bias calculation runs.
key_functions: _htResizeCompute — correctly computes new center position (center + deltaW/2)
_htResizeApplyCompound — positions children at calc.position + relX*scaleX (moves children to new center first)
_htResizeApplyCompound — sets min-width-bias-left='0%' to anchor left, but bias applies to already-moved children origin, not original NW corner
root_cause_analysis.invariant_that_holds: child.position relative to container.BB.x1 is preserved (child does not move within the container)
root_cause_analysis.invariant_that_breaks: container.BB.x1 (NW corner) is not anchored when dragging SE — it drifts in the drag direction

surgical_fix_guidance.approach: For a SE resize, the NW corner must be pinned BEFORE children are repositioned. Calculate the target BB from the anchored NW corner (not from the computed center), derive the new center from that, then reposition children relative to that derived center.
surgical_fix_guidance.formula: For SE resize: anchoredX1 = preContainer.x1 (fixed), newCenterX = anchoredX1 + newWidth/2. Replace calc.position.x with this value before the child reposition loop in _htResizeApplyCompound.
surgical_fix_guidance.general_rule: For any single-corner or single-edge resize: the OPPOSITE corner/edge should be fixed in place. The new center is derived from the fixed edge + new size/2, not from the node.position() + deltaSize/2.
